facts.material: reinforced marine-grade PVC, buoyant closed-cell foam, laminated LDPE bubble material
facts.function: floating platform that a vessel is driven onto to keep the hull out of water contact and reduce marine growth
facts.form: fully assembled floating structure, five sizes, moored to a berth with lines
facts.end_use: marina berths for recreational/commercial boats; not part of a vessel, not a dock or pier

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 8907 covers 'other floating structures' (rafts, tanks, cofferdams, landing-stages, buoys and beacons); the hull protector is a non-navigable floating structure moored at a berth
Section XVII note 2 / chapter 89: the article is not a part or accessory of a vessel (not attached to or forming part of a vessel), so no parts provision applies
GRI 1: a named heading for floating structures prevails over the residual plastics heading 3926 and 6307
GRI 6: 8907.90.00 other (not inflatable raft), statistical suffix .90 other (not buoys or tanks)

rejected_alternatives.reason: not an inflatable raft; buoyancy from closed-cell foam
residual articles of plastics; heading 8907 specifically describes floating structures
not a floating dock or vessel whose navigability is subsidiary to a main function; it is a simple moored floating platform, and the importer states it is not a dock

classification.rationale: The hull protector is a buoyant, non-navigable floating structure moored at a berth, which fits heading 8907 'other floating structures' under GRI 1. It is not a part of a vessel and not a dock of 8905. NY I87186 classified a modular floating system in 8907.90.0090, and the same statistical 'Other' line (not buoys or tanks) is used here.
